summary.headline: Jai Balaji Q2 FY27: revenue up 22% YoY, adjusted EBITDA up 93% to a ~9% margin, PAT nearly tripled, while DI pipe demand stays soft.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations up 22% YoY, adjusted EBITDA up 93% with margin around 9% (from 5%), and PAT up about 192%, with PAT margin around 5% (from 2%). H1 FY27 revenue grew 23%, adjusted EBITDA about 54% and PAT about 67%. Growth was attributed to specialised ferro alloys realisations, higher volumes in key commodity products and operational efficiency, while DI pipe demand remains subdued by slow government fund releases. Capex of about Rs 1,112 crore (mostly internally funded) is nearly complete, with blast furnace, ferro alloy and related expansions targeted for commissioning by end Q3 FY27.

financial_highlights.value: up about 192% YoY; PAT margin about 5%
up about 67% YoY; PAT margin about 5%

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 169 crore at end FY26
expected about Rs 140 crore by March 2027

financial_highlights.value: Rs 395 crore, plus Rs 137 crore additional facility from HDFC Bank

segments.name: DI pipes
segments.commentary: Demand soft for 4-5 quarters; order book about 80-90 thousand tonnes, about 50% price-indexed. Q2 production fell to about 37,000 tonnes from 41,000 in Q1 due to a physical capacity constraint in the open area. Surplus output is being sold as ductile iron/pig-type product at a reasonable margin.

segments.name: Specialised ferro alloys
segments.commentary: About 28% of Q2 revenue; management expects share to rise to about 30-31%. Margins of 50-60% cited as normative, with realisations improving over recent quarters; management does not expect further margin expansion.

segments.name: Commodity / billets / TMT
segments.commentary: Production improved in pig iron, billets and TMT in the quarter; other categories broadly stable. Q2 volumes were down 3-4% in value terms due to planned maintenance on one business unit.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 FY27 to be better than H1, with DI pipe demand recovery likely to take 1-2 quarters at the earliest, tied to release of government funds (Jal Jeevan Mission budget of Rs 67,000 crore, of which about Rs 16,500 crore spent to date).
Blast furnace and ferro alloy capacity expansions to commission by end Q3 FY27; blast furnace module expected to lift current blast furnace output efficiency by about 25-30%.
Gross debt to fall from Rs 188 crore to about Rs 140 crore by March 2027, potentially to Rs 110 crore depending on cash surplus.
Working capital facility cost expected to fall from about 12% to about 7% under the HDFC arrangement; management is also in talks with PSU banks next quarter.
Ferro alloy EBITDA margin expected to reach about 10-10.5% overall with new capacity; absolute EBITDA to rise with volumes.
capex_capacity: DI pipe capacity expanded to more than 5.5 lakh tonnes per annum; demand, not capacity, is the constraint. Utilisation about 40%; economic attractiveness requires 60-70%.

Specialised ferro alloy capacity to rise from 1.66 lakh to 1.9 lakh tonnes per annum (about 25-30 thousand tonnes added), with current utilisation about 90%; incremental revenue potential cited as about Rs 490 crore.
Blast furnace capacity to rise from 6.3 lakh to 7.5 lakh tonnes; central capacity from 9 lakh to about 12 lakh tonnes (figures as stated in call, may be mis-transcribed).
Overall Rs 1,112 crore investment programme nearly complete, funded predominantly by internal accruals; Rs 36 crore deployed in Q2 FY27. Dedicated railway siding supports logistics.
Management said further group-level investment plans are on the drawing board and will be announced later; details not yet finalised.
demand_pricing: Government ordering is the key driver for DI pipes; slow fund release means contractors are reluctant to add funding to execute contracts. Management expects FY28 spending to improve as AMRUT 2.0 and JJM (extended to March 2028) funds flow.
Ferro alloy demand described as robust; specialised products command a premium over benchmark prices; exports to more than 40-45 countries with stocking in Europe and the US.

DI pipe pricing: management says the sharp price correction happened last quarter and prices are now stabilising, with marginal improvement expected as cooking coal costs rise and producers cut output.
Raw material pass-through: commodity products reprice within about 15-20 days; specialised products within about 2-3 months, with price increases already passed through since last month.
Inland waterway and river-linking projects expected to require DI pipes, but tenders are still at DPR stage; inquiries expected from next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for enhanced capacity to reach optimal utilisation and incremental revenue over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said blast furnace upgrade should cut cost and lift current blast furnace output by about 25-30%; it will also integrate operations that are not fully integrated. No firm revenue figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company expanding into specialised alloy steel for railways?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment plans are still on the drawing board and will be proposed at group level, including other investment companies; details to be announced in a later phase.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade payables and other liabilities drive a cash outflow of about Rs 290 crore in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited inventory build of about Rs 200 crore and around Rs 70-60 crore of debt repayment. Exact figures were not available to the speaker.

qa_highlights.question: Targeted net debt over the next 12-18 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt to fall to about Rs 140 crore by March 2027 and potentially Rs 110 crore depending on cash surplus; net debt was Rs 145 crore at the end of Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How will the new working capital lines improve liquidity and cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation previously around 70% expected to fall; packing credit from HDFC Bank reduces cost from about 12% to about 7%. Bank mix is shifting from NBFCs to private banks (Kotak, HDFC).

qa_highlights.question: What DI pipe order book and export exposure exist?
qa_highlights.answer: DI order book about 80-90 thousand tonnes, about 50% price-indexed. Exports are small; management expects exports to grow with ferro alloy and DI capacity expansions.

qa_highlights.question: What utilisation would make expanded DI pipe capacity economical, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Economic attractiveness needs about 60-70% utilisation versus about 40% now. Management expects only a gradual recovery over 1-2 quarters, with bigger gains in FY28.

risks_watch: Prolonged slow government fund release delaying DI pipe order recovery; DI utilisation about 40%.
Rising raw material costs (cooking coal), with pass-through lags of 2-3 months on specialised products; geopolitical uncertainty.
Inventory build (about Rs 200 crore) and a Rs 290 crore operating cash outflow in H1; working-capital dependence on bank limits.
Commissioning of blast furnace and ferro alloy capacity by end Q3 FY27 and ramp-up timing.
Sustainability of specialised ferro alloy realisations, which management says are unlikely to expand further.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the specialised ferro alloy business and margins, but cautious on DI pipe demand, with management repeatedly saying near-term recovery is slow and dependent on government fund release. Several answers on capacity, investment plans and export opportunities were vague or incomplete.
key_quotes: JVIL delivered a strong performance in Q2 FY27 with revenue growth of 22 percent year over year and with EBITDA nearly doubling and PAT increasing threefold year over year.
While near-term demand continues to remain subdued, our expanded capacity of 5.5 lakh tons per annum is readily available to support higher volumes as the market conditions improve gradually.
We are not looking at the expanding the margin so we have to say 5 points or 10 points more if we are able to maintain this we will be pretty happy.

growth.why: Management expects H2 FY27 better than H1 with ferro alloy and blast furnace capacity commissioning by end Q3 FY27 (about 1 quarter out, given Q2 call), and ferro alloy utilisation ~90% supports volume, but no explicit revenue growth % was guided and DI pipe demand is soft with utilisation only ~40%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides overall EBITDA margin to about 10-10.5% from about 9% in Q2 as ferro alloy (50-60% normative margin, ~28% of revenue rising to 30-31%) and blast furnace efficiency gains (25-30%) come through.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Blast furnace (6.3 to 7.5 lakh tpa), ferro alloy (1.66 to 1.9 lakh tpa, ~25-30 kt added, ~90% utilisation) and central capacity expansions are under construction with commissioning targeted by end Q3 FY27; Rs 1,112 crore programme nearly complete.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects H2 FY27 better than H1; ferro alloy utilisation ~90% and new capacity lifts volumes, but DI pipe utilisation is only ~40% and DI recovery is 1-2 quarters at the earliest, so growth is concentrated in ferro alloys.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Further group-level investment plans are on the drawing board and to be announced later with details not finalised; no firm amount or date given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects H2 better than H1 and EBITDA margin rising to 10-10.5%, but gave no explicit revenue growth percentage and DI demand recovery is conditional on government fund release.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: DI pipe demand soft for 4-5 quarters with utilisation ~40% and Q2 DI output down to ~37 kt from 41 kt; slow government fund release and cooking coal cost rises are key risks, and commissioning/ramp-up timing could slip.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product launch was firmly guided; alloy steel for railways is still only on the drawing board with details to be announced in a later phase.

rows.label: Gross debt down to about Rs 140 crore by March 2027
rows.why: Gross debt falls from Rs 188 crore in Q2 to about Rs 140 crore by March 2027, potentially Rs 110 crore, with net debt already at Rs 145 crore versus Rs 169 crore at FY26 end.

rows.label: Working capital cost cut to about 7% via HDFC
rows.why: Packing credit cost expected to fall from about 12% to about 7% under the HDFC arrangement on Rs 395 crore limits plus Rs 137 crore extra facility; PSU bank talks next quarter.

rows.label: Inventory build unwinds after Rs 290 crore H1 outflow
rows.why: H1 operating cash outflow of about Rs 290 crore driven by about Rs 200 crore inventory build; no explicit unwind timing was guided.

tone.note: Management was confident on specialised ferro alloy margins, capacity commissioning by end Q3 FY27 and deleveraging, but cautious on DI pipe demand which it said recovers slowly and depends on government fund release; Q&A on investment plans, exports and the Rs 290 crore cash outflow was vague.

quality.why: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 22% YoY, led by specialised ferro alloy realisations (about 28% of Q2 revenue, margins 50-60%) plus higher commodity volumes, while DI pipes stayed soft at about 40% utilisation; the brief gives no one-off items, but the ferro alloy price-led margin gain is not expected to expand further and the brief does not split revenue growth between price and volume.
